subject.title: [Bug]: /context detail shows ~62k untracked provider/runtime overhead on fresh OpenAI Codex gpt-5.5 session

question: How should `/context detail` classify Codex app-server token totals when they exceed OpenClaw's tracked prompt estimate: context-window occupancy, billing/accounting usage, native thread/provider overhead, or unknown residual?
rationale: Source and upstream Codex contracts show the current buckets are insufficient, but choosing labels and compaction semantics requires maintainer intent plus live Codex evidence rather than an autonomous guess.

options.title: Build the provider-aware ledger
options.body: Use live Codex OAuth proof to map each reported token field into measured, provider-reported, estimated, or unknown buckets before changing user-facing labels or compaction inputs.

options.title: Keep the generic residual for now
options.body: Document that the value is a conservative unknown overhead and defer compaction-semantic changes until Codex exposes clearer attribution.

options.title: Defer the issue
options.body: Leave the issue open but blocked on upstream Codex token semantics or additional reporter evidence from a current-main run.

recommendation.title: Build the provider-aware ledger
recommendation.body: Use live Codex OAuth proof to map each reported token field into measured, provider-reported, estimated, or unknown buckets before changing user-facing labels or compaction inputs.
